problem: Existing skill self-evolution methods were built for digital environments and turn trajectories into coarse whole-skill rewrites. In embodied tasks a failure may be an execution lapse (the agent ignored valid guidance) rather than a wrong skill, so coarse updates add redundancy, overwrite valid content or keep wrong content.
motivation: Embodied environments vary in layout, object states and visibility, so an initial skill cannot cover every situation and must evolve from the agent's own trajectories. Trajectory outcomes are entangled with perception, grounding and execution reliability, so the update signal must say which skill content is implicated and why.
key_idea: Reflect on each trajectory against the current skill and classify it as Discovery, Optimization, Skill Defect or Execution Lapse, so that only implicated skill-body content is edited and lapses only update a reminder appendix.
insight: Making skill updates skill-aware and targeted matters more than merely updating the skill. On ALFWorld with Qwen3.5-27B and GPT-5.2 as the skill model, the static skill gives 73.13, skill-unaware evolution 78.36 and EmbodiSkill 93.28. Skill-unaware evolution also converges lower and fluctuates more across revision stages. Separating execution-lapse evidence into an appendix avoids corrupting valid content, but the paper has no ablation isolating the appendix from the typed reflections.
method: Skill representation: the skill is S=(S_body, S_app), where the body holds prescriptive procedures and the appendix only highlights valid body content that should be followed carefully

Skill-aware reflection: after each trajectory, the skill evolution model F produces up to K reflections (K=1) with type, evidence, directive and target content; success gives Discovery or Optimization, failure gives SkillDefect or ExecutionLapse

Reflection consolidation: after B valid reflections, they are partitioned by type, and Discovery, Optimization and SkillDefect reflections are deduplicated, merged, grouped by target and conflict-resolved (misplaced or unresolvable ones are reassigned or discarded)

Constrained body revision: F acts as a constrained editor that adds Discovery content and modifies only the targets named by Optimization and SkillDefect, leaving other content unchanged apart from light consistency edits
Appendix update: ExecutionLapse reflections never change the body; they are merged with the old appendix and anchored to the updated body, with duplicates and obsolete items removed
Skill-aware evolution spiral: the revised skill guides later executions, which yield new trajectories for further revision; the executor is frozen and the skill is fixed at test time

setting.backbone: Frozen executors (Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct) with skill evolution model GPT-5.2 or Gemini-3-flash (frozen, prompted)
setting.training_data: No parameter training; the skill is evolved from trajectories on training tasks (ALFWorld 3,553 tasks; EB-Habitat 1,000; EB-Navigation 1,000) over 10 revision stages
setting.observation: ALFWorld text observations; EmbodiedBench visual observations (egocentric images) with task instructions
setting.action_space: High-level discrete text/embodied actions of ALFWorld and EmbodiedBench (Habitat high-level skills, Navigation discrete moves)
setting.privileged: none at test time (the skill is evolved on training tasks with binary success signals, then fixed)

numbers_note: Custom train/test splits on ALFWorld and EmbodiedBench, not the standard navigation benchmarks. Only task success is reported.
results: With Qwen3.5-27B and GPT-5.2 as the skill model, EmbodiSkill reaches 93.28% on ALFWorld, above G-Memory (74.62), direct GPT-5.2 (70.89) and direct Gemini-3-flash (82.09). On EmbodiedBench with Qwen3-VL-32B it gets 52.33 on Habitat and 61.33 on Navigation, beating memory baselines and direct agents, though the 8B executor is weaker on Navigation than some baselines (50.33 vs 47.00 for LangMem is still higher, but far below GPT-5.2's 57.33).
limitations: Evaluation covers only ALFWorld and EmbodiedBench with a binary success signal and a single small test split; navigation gains are modest and long-horizon navigation stays low

Depends on strong closed-source models (GPT-5.2, Gemini-3-flash) to evolve skills, so cost and reproducibility are concerns; results vary by skill model (Qwen3.5-27B with Gemini gains only +1.49 over skill-unaware)
No ablation isolates the appendix or consolidation, and no analysis of skill length or of transfer across environments
